title: Return Faster
headline: Spiritual Maturity Means Returning to God Faster
headline_sub: That’s Not Where I Live Anymore
tagline: Maturity may be measured by how quickly you come back.
seo_title: Spiritual Maturity: Returning to God Faster (Luke 15:17-20) | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Maturity isn't never wandering; it's recognizing sooner and returning faster. A devotional for men on the prodigal son and Romans 8:1.
verse_text: When he came to his senses…. “I will set out and go back to my father.” So he got up and went to his father.

scriptures.text: When he came to his senses…. “I will set out and go back to my father.” So he got up and went to his father.
Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.

blocks.text: But what if one evidence of increasing maturity is also this:
You recognize sooner when you have wandered, and you return more quickly.

items: It once took three days before you realized bitterness had taken over your thinking.
Eventually the thought arrives, and almost immediately something within you recognizes:
But because you’ve become increasingly familiar with the Vine.

sections.label: The Prodigal Son Shows Us Something

items: Luke records an extraordinary phrase: “When he came to his senses….”
Something happened internally before anything changed externally.
He could have sat in the pigpen analyzing himself.

blocks.text: He could have spent another six months becoming extremely self-aware…. while remaining in the pigpen.

items: “So he got up and went to his father.”

sections.label: Don’t Build a House in the Pigpen of Self-Analysis

items: Identifying the thought isn’t the goal.
Understanding your trigger isn’t the goal.
Awareness is valuable because it gives us an opportunity to turn.
Conviction tells you what’s wrong so you’ll return.
Condemnation tells you what’s wrong so you’ll hide.
It’s recognizing sooner when you’ve wandered and returning to Christ more quickly.
